data.title: Workbench Kit
data.description:
The prototype of the Workbench Kit: a parser for a JavaScript subset, a typed IR, emitters, and the tooling around them, so that a workbench (a domain language, an IDE, an agent and a book) can be built from a few small generated files instead of being regenerated whole every time.

Proposal: project/2026-11-23-workbench-kit-proposal.md. Rulings: project/2026-11-23-delivery-decisions.md. Platform findings: project/2026-11-23-m0-platform-probe.md.

data.title: M1: Game slice
data.description:
Tests hypotheses H1 (runtime lambdas fit comfortably in the subset) and H10 (the IR earns its keep) on a real grammar: the DMG Workbench's. Each runtime lambda in a preset is parsed from String(fn), lowered to IR and emitted as JS, then swapped into the DMG runtime in place of the original closure. Seeded traces of the original and swapped runs are compared.

Plan and binding decisions: project/2026-11-23-m1-game-slice-plan.md.

data.title: Typed IR, DMG dialect description, and lowering
data.description:
Why: the IR is meant to be the single source of truth that every backend, check and view reads (proposal §5). In the DMG Workbench, nothing depends on its IR, and behavior lives in opaque closures (finding L4, confirmed in project/2026-11-23-dmg-workbench-read.md). This leaf makes runtime behavior into data.

What:
- kit/ir/: a small typed IR with a diffable JSON form. It has types, functions, kernels (a function plus the domain it runs over), effects recorded on statements, and spans on every node.
- A lowering pass from the parser's AST, which resolves names and types against a dialect description and emits diagnostics: undeclared free variable, unknown member, type mismatch, effect not allowed in this domain.
- A DMG dialect description written in the kit's terms. Its inputs: the types of `self` (attributes with their types, baked constants, built-ins `x y index world alive visible`), the `w` surface the presets use (`frame`, `param`, `rand`, `rng.pick`, `board.at`/`filter`, `pool`, `spawn`, `emit`, `sfx`, `toast`, `input.*`, `grid.step`), `at(c,r).text` printf, and `Math.*`. Read attribute types from the built spec; keep the description beside the oracle harness or in kit/dialects/dmg/.

Already decided: integer semantics must match the oracle. Coercion happens on store, and an assignment expression evaluates to the unwrapped value, so `--self.ttl` on a u8 holding 0 yields −1 while 255 is stored. How the IR represents that is this leaf's call. Write the choice into the plan doc. Predicate lambdas to declared query intrinsics are allowed when they are pure. Strings are runtime values in this grammar (sprite names, choice params, event names), and so are entity references that may be empty.

Open, agent's call: whether a reference interpreter over the IR earns a place in M1. The proposal (§12) wants one eventually, but here the DMG runtime is the oracle. Ask the user before widening the subset beyond the predicate case.

Strictly test-first.

Out of scope: the emitter; GLSL, wasm and C.

Risk: return types like `"up" | {sprite, y} | null` and variadic printf may push the type system past what §5.2 lists. Record each such case for the H1 report rather than forcing it.

data.title: JavaScript emitter
data.description:
Why: the JS backend runs natively in the browser and is the code every other backend is compared against (proposal §6). Its output replaces the original closures in the differential run.

What: kit/emit/js/ turns an IR kernel into the source of a plain JS function with the same calling convention as the DMG slot it replaces: `(self, w)`, `(w, data)`, and so on. It carries the dialect's numeric rules and keeps a line map from emitted code back to source spans. Emitted code may call the DMG runtime's own `self`/`w` proxies; the point is to prove the lowering, not to replace the host.

Strictly test-first: unit tests per IR construct, then the emitted functions for presets 04–07, each checked against the oracle closure on recorded inputs where a whole-run trace would hide the cause.

Out of scope: other backends, optimization passes, and replacing the DMG runtime.

criteria.label: Every lowered lambda in presets 04–07 emits a function that the JS engine accepts (test).
Each emitted function maps every line back to its source span (test).
kit/emit/js/ imports no Node built-ins.

data.title: Differential run and H1/H10 report
data.description:
Why: this is M1's definition of done. It answers whether the approach works on a real grammar, and how comfortable the subset is, before any kit is extracted.

What:
- A script in scripts/ that, for presets 04–07, swaps every lowerable lambda for its emitted version and compares traces against the original. Use several seeds and generated input traces, over enough frames to reach game over where a game has one.
- The same script runs the lowering-only survey over all 22 presets: per preset, lambdas lowered, rejected with each reason, and the rewrites that would make each rejection lower.
- A dated findings doc in project/ that gives the verdict on H1 and H10, the subset widenings the evidence supports, and what M2 and M3 should change. Every figure names the command that reproduces it.
- The same doc corrects, in place, the proposal's errors listed in project/2026-11-23-dmg-workbench-read.md, each as a marked block quote. These are L5's overstated C coverage, L11's `lab:` links, L2's "mutation mode", the preset ids, and §5.8's wrap-before-compare.

Out of scope: fixing rejected presets by changing the DMG grammar.

criteria.label: For presets 04–07, every swapped run matches the original trace across the chosen seeds and input traces, or each mismatch is explained in the findings doc (script output).
The findings doc gives lowered/rejected counts for all 22 presets with reasons, and the command that reproduces them.
The proposal's factual errors are corrected in place as marked block quotes.

data.title: Oracle review fixes: trace coverage, bot input, test pinning
data.description:
Why: an independent review of b4f3b83 found that the oracle's traces miss differences a swapped lambda can cause, so a "match" in the M1 differential run would prove less than it claims. All findings were confirmed by red probes in the session scratchpad (review-oracle/gaps.test.mjs, P1–P8; mutate.sh for the test-pinning gap).

What (one surface: scripts/dmg-oracle/, tsconfig.json):
- S1: runTrace never calls rt.botInput(), so bot lambdas (presets 13, 20–24) never run and swapping one always matches. Add a way to drive input from the bot.
- M1: renderEvery defaults to 0, so draw/hud swaps (10 of 25 lambdas in presets 04–07) go undetected by default. Make the default exercise render.
- M2: TraceOptions.params throws (the DMG Runtime constructor calls set() before this.log exists). Make it work or remove it.
- M3: 16 of 22 single-line mutations leave the oracle suite green: trace fields (entity v, x/y, visible, alive, bg hash, bg scroll, oamStart, over/reason, fb hash, log data), rt.err ignored, firstDifference over min(len) ticks, no-op swaps for addRecord slots (methods, draw, done, bot) and for `every`, bot/inits omitted from lambdaSlots. Add a "changing X changes the trace" test per field and a swap test per slot kind.
- M4: 10 of 126 inventory lambdas reference top-level helpers/constants (DIRS, placeFood, scramble, …); the inventory doesn't flag this, so parse coverage is overstated. Flag it in the inventory and README.
- M5: skipLibCheck: true disables type-checking of the project's own .d.ts files.
- Minor: RNG draws not recorded (m1); bg hash covers tile indices, not glyph meaning (m2); snapshot of an event payload holding an entity proxy throws (m3); JSON snapshots merge NaN/null, undefined/absent, -0/0 (m4); timer `after` lambdas not listed or swappable (m5); firstDifference names `frame` instead of `error` on an erroring tick (m6).

data.title: Parser review fixes: spans, over-acceptance, fixits
data.description:
Why: an independent review of 9da34d4 found the parser builds wrong spans and accepts input JavaScript rejects or reads differently, and some fixits change meaning. Lowering and the emitter's line map trust this tree, so it is fixed before KHQFvD builds on it. Red probes: session scratchpad review-parser/probes.test.js (F1–F22, F12b, F16b; all 24 fail today), spans-corpus.mjs (23 of 3456 corpus expression spans don't compile alone), table.mjs, mutate.sh (18 of 21 mutants survive the suite).

Serious:
- S1: a node whose first operand is parenthesized starts its span inside the paren (parser.js:85-88, 283). Breaks the S104 fixit too.
- S2: the S104 template fixit doesn't parenthesize its concatenation: `a${b}`.length → "a" + (b).length.
- S3: `in` on plain objects (parser.js:123, 256; statements.js:30) makes valueOf/toString/constructor wrong nodes.

Moderate: M1 parseLambda throws (constructor outside try; RangeError on \u{110000}); M2 `??` mixed with ||/&& accepted; M3 legacy octal 010, "\1" mis-valued; M4 malformed numbers (1_, 0x, 1e) accepted, some as NaN; M5 reserved words as names; M6 parenthesized patterns and shorthand initializers outside patterns; M7 var→let fixit changes meaning under hoisting; M8 ==→=== fixit changes meaning; M9 S104 fixit mishandles CRLF and line continuations in templates.

Minor: N1 unicode identifier classes and line terminators (U+2028/9, lone CR); N2 newline before =>; N3 arrow as binary operand or callee; N4 assignment through an optional chain; N5 const without init, lexical decl as if body, for-of initializers, duplicate params/let; N6 HTML-like comments; N7 S116 fixit edits a comment; N8 TemplateElement ranges include delimiters; N9 over-strict P001s (trailing param comma, for(x in o), async(1)).

Rulings with Ben (2026-11-23): S116 keeps its warning and tip but loses its fixit. S112, S113, S114 are recorded as rejected in the plan's Parser rulings. M7: pending Ben's answer.

data.text:
IR leaf findings (irwright, 2026-11-23).

All 25 runtime lambdas in presets 04–07 lower to kernels with no diagnostics (scripts/dmg-lower/test/lower-corpus.test.js). An ad-hoc run of lowerPreset over all 22 presets lowered 104 of 126 (not a committed script; K4kgqD owns the survey).

Types past proposal §5.2, recorded for the H1 report (each was added rather than forced):
- str and string enums: sprite names, choice params, buttons, event and pool names. A string literal is a one-value enum; `"sweep"` vs choice `order` is checked against its options.
- Optional (possibly-empty) references: w.rng.pick, w.spawn, list.find. Lowering requires a check before use (narrowing on if (m), if (!m) return, m && …; const locals only), else L008.
- Union: the draw result, sprite-name | {sprite?, x?, y?, flipX?, flipY?} | null (presets 04–06); bot results; printf arguments (f64 | str | bool).
- Variadic printf: Cell.text(fmt: str, ...rest). The format string is not checked against the argument count.
- Lists with a maximum length (board 9, pool 24), so `each` loops are bounded; a list may carry extra members (the board's throwing `at`).
- Struct payloads and method signatures are inferred program-wide (DMG events and method params are untyped): payload from emit sites, params from call sites, result and effects from the method body, iterated to a fixed point.
- Keyed functions: w.param("x"), w.spawn("pool"), w.pool, w.sfx, w.all, w.one; the literal key selects the signature (L011 otherwise).

Reference interpreter: not in M1. The DMG runtime running the original closure is the oracle for every lambda, so an interpreter would be a third implementation checked against the same oracle and would test nothing H1 or H10 asks. It earns its place when a backend has no closure to compare with (GLSL in M2, or D1 operators); then it should be written against these IR goldens.

Gaps the 22-preset survey will show as rejections that are the lowering's, not the subset's: destructuring, for…of, array literals, `let x;`, `??`, reduce without an initial value (13 bot), string methods (.repeat 11, .toUpperCase 30) as L002, w.bg (21, 22, 26) not in the dialect, writes to w.oamStart (24, 30: the host's rule is (v|0)&255, not a declared store type) as L013, baked arrays/objects left out of the dialect.

JS emitter findings (irwright, 2026-11-23).

kit/emit/js emits every one of the 25 lowered lambdas in presets 04–07; each instantiates, and swapped alone into a fresh build, matches the original trace over 600 frames (seed 7, inputTrace(7, 600), renderEvery 4). Command: node --test scripts/dmg-lower/test/emit-oracle.test.js (about 1.2 s).

Numeric rules: values are JS doubles; a store is a plain assignment through the DMG proxy, which applies the attribute's coercion and logs its warnings (the trace compares those logs, so coercing in emitted code too would be wrong only in the logs, never silently). Recorded in the plan doc, "Integer semantics in the IR".

Sensitivity probe (ad hoc, not committed): mutating each emitted lambda (=== to !==, + to -, > to >=, return to return void, ! to !!) and re-running the same check caught 26 of 32 mutants. The 6 missed: > to >= on Mole.draw (05), Countdown.onFrame (06) and Spark.onFrame (07), whose boundary values never occur in 600 frames; return null to return undefined in 05 Mole.draw and return false to undefined in 06 whack, both equivalent to the host; and 06 done, which first fires at frame 2400. For K4kgqD: run long enough to reach game over, with several seeds.

data.title: IR review fixes: receiver evaluation, order, loop bounds, codes
data.description:
Why: an independent review of f8f6d3d found that compound assignment and ++/-- evaluate a non-stable receiver twice (duplicating RNG draws), plus ordering, loop-bound, reason-code and IR-spec gaps, and 13 of 24 semantic mutants that survive the suite. None of the 22 presets hits S1 today, but the IR's guarantees (left-to-right evaluation, bounded loops) must hold before the differential report leans on them. Probes: session scratchpad review-ir/ (h.js helper; p1, p2, p6, p7, p8, p10, p11, p12 are the reproductions).

Serious:
- S1: assign.js:28, 59-62, 102-104 re-evaluate the receiver for compound assignment and ++/--: `w.board.at(w.rng.int(9)).ttl += 30` emits two RNG draws (p1, p10).
Moderate:
- M1: compound assignment reads its target after the right side's spilled statements (assign.js:50, 62): `self.ttl += (self.ttl = 5)` gives 8 vs 10 (p2).
- M2: L007 checks only the test's shape; `for (let i = -1e17; i < 4; i++)` lowers and never ends (stmt.js:150-176, p7).
- M3: semantic tests are thin: 13 of 24 one-line mutants survive (p8); the find test (emit.test.js:77-83) passes for the wrong reason; empty-list some/every untested.
- M4: list indexing is reported as L009 but documented as L012 (expr.js:150, call.js:37); w.oamStart / w.over writes are rejected as L013 though the runtime's world set trap accepts them (dialects/dmg/index.js:96-97), presets 24 and 30.
- M5: `present` is used for any optional (f64?, bool?) but specified as "tests an optional"; it means JS truthiness (ir.d.ts:86, expr.js:312, p11).
Minor: m1 reduce evaluates init before its list (query.js:40,71); m2 a callback assigning an enclosing let gets no L006; m3 L004 bypassed via a method that fails to lower (failed() gives effects: []) and self-recursive methods; m4 browser-safe test misses `import "node:fs"`, dynamic import, `from"x"`, and relative imports leaving kit/ (p12); m5 ir.d.ts:35 and the plan say clamp-truncate-wrap but the host truncates then clamps (Runtime.prototype.coerce ~line 1216); m6 line map tested only for bounds; m7 `return w.end("crash")` in onFrame rejected as L003.

criteria.label: Every reproduction in review-ir/ (p1, p2, p6, p7, p11, p12) behaves correctly as a repo test
Each surviving mutant in review-ir/p8-mutants.mjs is killed, or its survival is explained
Reason codes and docs match: L009/L012 for indexing, world writes, present, coercion order

data.text:
irfix, D8Sv9n findings (2026-11-23), worktree agent-acb91cd0edae15b15.

Fixed, each with a red test first (kit/emit/js/test/semantics.test.js, kit/lower/test/review.test.js):

- S1/M1: placeFor({ once }) saves a non-stable receiver to a temp for compound assignment and ++/--; compound assignment now reads the target via seq([load, rhs]) so the old value is saved before a spilling right side (locals too: `a += (a = 5)` gives 6).
- m1: reduce saves a non-stable list to a temp when its init is also non-stable, so the list is evaluated first.
- M2: L007 unless the counter starts at a safe-integer literal (negation allowed) or w.param(...), and a constant bound is within 2^53. All presets' loops still lower (`dy = -1` included).
- M4: `list[i]` is L012 ("Indexing a list is not lowered yet"), any other computed name L009; README and code agree. w.oamStart (store u8) and w.over (store bool) are writable, read effects renamed `read World.over` / `read World.oamStart`. Preset 24's lambda now lowers: 105 of 126 lower, 21 rejected; all 105 match the original swapped alone on seeds 7 and 11 at 1200 frames (reviewer's p5 pointed at the worktree).
- M5: `present` only for opt of an entity ref (or union of refs); everything else is `truthy`. ir.d.ts says so.
- m2: assigning or updating any local inside a query callback is L006.
- m3: method sigs carry `calls` and `partial` (it or a callee failed). A draw/hud/every/after or a callback calling a partial method gets L014; a method on a call cycle gets L007 at the call.
- m4: browser-safe test rewritten around problems(text, file): bare import, `from"x"`, dynamic import(), require, and relative imports that leave kit/; JSDoc comments stripped first. Probe p12's strings are its own test.
- m5: ir.d.ts and the plan corrected (truncate, clamp, wrap) with a marked block quote.
- m6: line map test now checks statement spans exactly (kills mutant S).
- m7: `return f()` in a void slot lowers to do + return when f() is void.

Mutants (review-ir/p8-mutants.mjs, re-run on a copy of the worktree): all 24 killed or, for W, the pattern no longer exists (assign.js was rewritten); its replacements W2 (member) and W3 (local) are both killed, as are 9 new mutants of the fixes (Z1-Z9).

irfix, K4kgqD findings (2026-11-23), worktree agent-acb91cd0edae15b15. Report: project/2026-11-23-m1-findings.md; tool: scripts/dmg-diff/ (survey, diff, mutants verbs).

- Differential: `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js diff` — 10 cases over 04-07 (params: 04 sweep, 04 spawn 150 + sound off, 05 linger override 2.5, 07 burst/gravity extremes; plus "04 linger 0 (edited)", a derived program that makes the u16 wrap reachable) x seeds 7, 11, 23 x 3000 frames, each lambda alone and all at once: 30 runs, 0 differences. 06 done fires on every seed (over 601/156/601 ticks). Prerelease suite: scripts/dmg-diff/prerelease/diff.prerelease.js, 34 s.
- The shipped 04's wrap path is unreachable: linger's slider clamps overrides to 0.5, so ttl >= 30.
- Mutants: `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js mutants` — 9 p13 mutants: 5 caught, 4 equivalent under the host (reasons in sensitivity.js). y > 144 vs >= caught only by burst 6 on 2 of 3 seeds.
- Survey: `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js survey` — 126 lambdas: 105 lowered, 11 helpers (= inventory topLevelRefs), 9 not-yet (L012/L002/L015-on-reduce), 1 subset (23 bot, L007 step 8). Preset 02 has no runtime lambdas. Pinned in scripts/dmg-diff/test/dmg-diff.test.js.
- Proposal corrected in place (L2, L5, L11, §5.8 + preset 10 u16, preset ids under the roadmap); the DMG read's coercion order also corrected.
- Verdicts: H1 yes for the simpler half, open for the games (20-26: 14 of 21 rejections); H10 supported narrowly (closures removed for 04-07 headless; IR answered effects/order/bounds/store questions; one level falls short on coercion, inlined queries, present/truthy). Who owns passes: evidence leans to the passes note's middle path; left for Ben.

data.title: dmg-diff review fixes: guard the swap path, early stops, classifier gaps
data.description:
Why: an independent review of scripts/dmg-diff (35c4547) found nothing that undoes M1's figures, but the path that produces the headline number is unguarded. Probes were in the session scratchpad review-diff/ (may be gone; the reproductions are restated here).

1. No test checks that runCase actually swaps: changing differential.js:119 to swap into a fresh build nobody runs (`swapLambda(make().spec, s.id, s.fn)`) leaves npm test and the prerelease suite green. The smoke test counts emitted functions, not swaps. Red test: plant a fault through runCase (an emit hook or one MUTANTS entry) and expect a mismatch for that slot and for `*`.
3. A run that stops early on a runtime error reports a clean match: DiffResult records neither ticks run nor the error, and the CLI prints the requested frame count (differential.js:114-130, cli.js:59). Record ticks run and errors; fail when a run stops short.
4. 9 of the 30 runs are repeats (04 sweep, 05 default, 05 linger 2.5 are seed-independent): report distinct runs (24) or vary input/seed meaningfully; "ten param settings" includes 3 defaults and 1 edited program.
5. `mutants --json` always exits 0 (cli.js:72) against README line 12; an "equivalent" mutant that some run catches prints "caught" without flagging the wrong equivalence claim (cli.js:75,79).
6. 07 break->continue equivalence reason is wrong: a full-pool w.spawn logs "pool 'sparks' is full" once (seed 7: 998 failed spawns, 1 warning); fix the reason in sensitivity.js.
7. Survey classifier: kit/lower/stmt.js:40-42 doesn't lower a for...of body, hiding errors in it (23 Bird.onFrame hides an L002 for w.bg); survey.js:25 counts every L002 (typos too) as not-yet; survey.js:47 counts arity errors on filter/find/some/every as not-yet though its comment says reduce only.
8. Latent: runCase (differential.js:111) and probe (sensitivity.js:51) swap only the first part's emitted function for a fragment lambda used by several parts; no preset has one today.
9. "Each of the 105 lowered lambdas, swapped in alone, matches on seeds 7 and 11 over 1200 frames" has no committed command; add one (e.g. a `diff --all-presets` verb in the prerelease suite, ~15 s).

data.description:

- Improve L007's tip for a non-unit step: suggest the counted rewrite.

data.title: Rule on the next H1 gates: array literals, w.bg, call-site type joins
data.description:
Why: after the widenings (96954db), 2 of 11 helper lambdas lower, not the ~7 expected. The remaining gates on H1 for the games are mostly two things, plus one inference limit. Each needs a ruling from Ben before it is built.

1. Array literals are not lowered. They block 20 Ball ([w.player, w.cpu]), 21 snake and its DIRS constant, 23 Bird ([[3,2],…]) and 25 at16. Tuple destructuring has nothing to destructure until they lower. The fork: type a literal as {list: T, max: n}, so each item is possibly empty (consistent with indexing), or add a fixed-length tuple type whose items are non-empty (more precise, and a new type in the core IR).
2. w.bg is not in the DMG dialect. It blocks 21 placeFood, 22 breakout.on(brick), 23 Bird, 25 flip, 26 Cursor, and probably 26 step. Describing it means typing the background API (cell reads and writes, scroll) and its effects. This is dialect work, not subset work.
3. Call-site typing for methods and helpers is first-wins. Two call sites that pass different string literals (enum types) mismatch at the second. Joining types across call sites would fix this for both.
Minor: a helper whose only callers fail to lower gets no call sites, so L014 says its parameters cannot be inferred. This is correct but noisy (writeCol).
Source: the m82n5e agent's report; counts from `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js survey`.

data.title: Rename Dialect to Environment and Kernel.domain to Iteration Space in code
data.description:
Why: Ben locked in the kit's terms on 2026-11-23 (project/2026-11-23-nomenclature.md, kit/glossary.md). Two code names now contradict them.

1. Lowering's `Dialect` (kit/lower/dialect.d.ts, `L.dialect`, `dmgDialect(declarationsOf(spec))`) is per Program: a Dialect plus one Program's declarations. It is the **Environment**. Rename the type, the file, fields, parameters and functions to match. Where the DMG code genuinely describes the DMG Dialect itself (static intrinsics, built-ins), keep "dialect"; the function that combines it with a Program's declarations builds an Environment.
2. `Kernel.domain` (kit/ir/ir.d.ts:144) and slot `domain` strings are the **Iteration Space**. Rename the field (e.g. `space`) through the IR, the JSON form, the listing, the emitter and the docs.
The IR goldens change with (2). That is an expected change, so update them and say why in the commit.
No behavior change. typecheck, npm test and the survey (107/9/3/7) stay as they are. Update the READMEs and remove the "rename is filed" notes from kit/glossary.md.

criteria.label: No code name contradicts kit/glossary.md for Environment or Iteration Space
No behavior change: typecheck, tests and survey figures unchanged

data.new_desc:
Why: after the subset widenings (96954db), most of the game presets' remaining rejections come down to three things. Ben ruled on all three on 2026-11-23; the rulings are in project/2026-11-23-m1-game-slice-plan.md, "Subset widenings after M1" (read them; they bind).

data.title: A list literal records its exact length, so constant indexes below it are never empty
data.description:
Why: Ben ruled on 2026-11-23 that a list literal records its exact length (the M1 plan, "Subset widenings after M1"). Bounded lists made every item of a literal possibly empty, even at a constant index below its length. That keeps 23 Bird.onFrame#0 rejected (`const [ox, oy] = …; self.x + ox`).

What: the type of `[a, b]` also carries its exact length (2), next to `max`. A constant index, or a destructuring position, below that length gives a non-empty item. Any other index, and any list without a known length (board, pools, filter results), stays possibly empty. There is still no tuple type. The strict join keeps lists of different lengths apart, as now.

Seams: the `array` node and list types in kit/ir (types.js, ir.d.ts), indexing in kit/lower/expr.js, tuple destructuring in kit/lower/pattern.js, and the survey pins in scripts/dmg-diff. Re-run the survey and `diff --all-presets` (0 differences required), re-pin the figures, and add a marked update to the M1 findings.

criteria.label: A constant index or destructuring position below a literal's length is non-empty, and every other index stays possibly empty, with tests
The survey and diff --all-presets are re-run (0 differences), and the figures are re-pinned and recorded

data.title: M2: Shader slice
data.description:
Tests H2 (a neutral core covers games and shaders) and H3 (typed operators make shader code pleasant without confusing authors). A tiny `fields` Dialect; one Kernel emitted to JS and GLSL; a comparison within a tolerance; the pixel debugger.

Plan, order and binding rulings: project/2026-11-23-m2-shader-slice-plan.md.

data.title: Survey the Uncommon Math fragment sketches and pick two for H3
data.description:
Why: H3 ports two of the book's fragment sketches both ways (typed operators, and plain-JS `add(mul(…))` calls) and compares them. The `fields` Dialect's intrinsics and Iteration Spaces should be the ones real sketches use, not guesses. This leaf picks the two sketches and lists what they need.

What: a dated finding, project/2026-11-2x-uncommon-math-sketches.md, that lists every fragment-style sketch in the book (a function evaluated per pixel or per point), and for each: its chapter, what it draws, its inputs and parameters, the operations it uses (vector arithmetic, swizzles, branches, loops and their bounds, noise, textures, state across frames), and whether it fits the Runtime Subset as it stands. Then a recommendation of two sketches for H3: one simple, one that exercises vectors and a bounded loop, with the reasons. Then the union of intrinsics and types those two need, which the `fields` Dialect leaf will implement.

Already decided: the source is local/uncommon-math-0.1.0.html, a gitignored 4.8 MB single-page app whose chapters are built from JS data; it lives only in the main checkout, so pass its absolute path (/Users/ben/git/workbench/local/uncommon-math-0.1.0.html) and never copy it into the repo. Extraction code, if any, goes in scripts/um-survey/ with a README, so the survey can be re-run.

Out of scope: designing the Dialect, porting anything. Risks: sketches may be written as canvas loops rather than per-pixel functions; say so, and say what that means for H3.

criteria.label: The finding lists every fragment-style sketch with its operations and subset fit, and names the command that reproduces the list
It recommends two sketches for H3 with reasons, and lists the intrinsics and types they need

data.title: An IR verifier, run after every lowering
data.description:
Why: M2 adds stages below the IR (the GLSL LIR) and new value types, and the passes ruling makes a verifier the safety net for every stage ([the passes note](../project/2026-11-23-passes-queries-and-several-irs.md); M1 findings, "What M2 and M3 should change"). M1 has none; its checks live inside lowering.

What: kit/ir/verify.js, `verify(kernel)` returning diagnostics (never throwing), checking the IR's own invariants as kit/ir/README.md states them: every expression's type agrees with its operands and its node kind; every name is bound before use; every statement's recorded effects cover what it does; loops are bounded; every node carries a span; the JSON form round-trips. Lowering (kit/lower) runs it on each Kernel it produces, behind a flag the tests turn on, and a failure is a kit bug (its own diagnostic code range, documented in kit/ir/README.md). All M1 goldens (scripts/dmg-lower) and every lowered lambda in the survey must pass it.

TDD: a test per invariant that builds a broken Kernel by hand and sees the right diagnostic, plus a test that every golden verifies.

Seams: kit/ir (new file), the call in kit/lower/index.js. Out of scope: rules for f32 and vectors (the value-types leaf adds them), and LIR rules (the GLSL leaf adds those). Risk: the verifier finds real bugs in M1's lowering; file each as an issue with --found-in this leaf rather than fixing it here, unless it is a one-line fix.

criteria.label: verify() reports each broken invariant with its own code, with a test per invariant
Every M1 golden and every lowered survey lambda verifies clean, and lowering runs the verifier under test

data.title: f32 and fixed-size vectors as IR value types
data.description:
Why: Ben ruled that `f32` and fixed-size vectors become IR value types; this is the one change M2 makes to the core, and H2's test of it. Shader code is vectors of f32 throughout, and typed operators (D1) need operand types to resolve on.

What: the IR's value types gain `f32` and `vec` of n = 2, 3 or 4 of a scalar type (at least f32), with the operations shaders need: componentwise arithmetic, scalar-times-vector, component access (`.x`, `.y`, and swizzles if the survey shows them), construction, and explicit conversions between f64 and f32. The JSON form, the listing (kit/ir/print.js) and the verifier understand them. Integer sizes stay on storage (store rules), as in M1. Today every value is f64; existing Kernels and goldens must not change.

Already decided: typed operators (D1, the proposal §5.7): `uv + k * q` on vectors means vector arithmetic. Nominal Dialect types: a Dialect's `vec2` and `color` never join even when both are three f32s (the strict-join ruling in the M1 plan, "Subset widenings after M1"); the IR may share a structural vector underneath, but lowering keeps the nominal names apart. No implicit f64↔f32 conversion anywhere; a mixed operation is a type error with a fix.

Open, the builder's call (record the choice and why in kit/ir/README.md): whether vector operations are typed `binary` nodes or intrinsic calls; how a nominal Dialect type maps to its structural vector.

Seams: kit/ir (types.js, ir.d.ts, json.js, print.js, verify.js), kit/lower where operator typing lives (expr.js). Not the backends: the JS-backend and GLSL leaves add emission. Record in this leaf's notes every change to existing M1 code, for H2's count.

criteria.label: The IR has f32 and vec2..4 types with arithmetic, access, construction and conversions, each with tests, and the verifier checks them
Every M1 golden is byte-identical and npm test passes, so the change did not disturb games

data.title: The fields Dialect, its Grammar, and typed operators in lowering
data.description:
Why: the second Dialect is H2's test (does the neutral core cover shaders?) and the vehicle for H3. It should be the smallest Dialect that carries the two sketches the survey chose.

What: kit/dialects/fields/ with a Dialect (types such as `vec2` and `color`, the `pixel` Iteration Space whose Kernel takes `uv` and returns a color, the intrinsics the survey listed, with each target's spelling) and a Grammar small enough to write a fields Program (one construct with `param` declarations and a `pixel` Runtime Lambda; the proposal's §8.1 and §8.2 sketch both). Lowering resolves operators on Dialect types (D1), so `uv * 2.0 + vec2(t, 0)` lowers to vector arithmetic, and a type error names the types and the fix. The two survey sketches, written as fields Programs, lower to Kernels that verify. Params are uniforms: constant across one frame, live between frames.

Already decided: D1 (typed operators; such Lambdas no longer run as plain JS); nominal types; no `Any`; the strict join for parameter types; the Library (intrinsics written in the Runtime Subset, such as `fbm`) lowers like any helper, so it reaches every backend (glossary: Library).

Seams: kit/dialects/fields (new), kit/lower (operator resolution; keep DMG behavior identical), kit/lower/environment.d.ts if the Environment needs a new shape. Look at kit/dialects/dmg for the existing pattern before inventing a new one. Record every change to existing M1 code in this leaf's notes, for H2.

Out of scope: backends; the Definition API's generic `.construct()` machinery (M3, H4), so hand-written builders are fine here.

criteria.label: Both survey sketches lower from fields Programs to Kernels that verify, with tests
Operator type errors name both types and a fix, with tests; the DMG survey and goldens are unchanged

data.title: A reference interpreter over the IR
data.description:
Why: with typed operators a fields Lambda has no runnable closure, so something must say what a Kernel means. Ben ruled that a reference interpreter over the IR is M2's oracle; the JS and GLSL outputs are each compared against it (floats within D5's tolerance, integers exactly). The proposal's §12 asks for "a small, slow, obviously correct interpreter".

What: kit/interp/, `run(kernel, inputs, env)` that evaluates a Kernel by walking the IR, with f64 as JS doubles, f32 rounded with Math.fround after every operation, vectors componentwise, and the M1 integer store rules. Intrinsics come from the Dialect (each intrinsic gets a reference implementation, kept separate from the JS backend's spelling so the two can disagree and be caught). Pure Kernels are the requirement. Then, as its own test of fidelity, it runs the M1 Kernels whose effects the DMG harness can supply and agrees with the emitted JS on a seeded trace; if effectful Kernels prove costly, stop at pure ones and say why in a note.

Obviously correct beats fast: no optimization, no sharing of code with kit/emit/js beyond the IR types.

Seams: kit/interp (new), kit/dialects/* for intrinsic reference implementations. Out of scope: stepping UI (the pixel debugger leaf builds on this, so expose a hook per evaluated node with its span).

criteria.label: The interpreter runs pure Kernels over f64, f32 and vectors, with a test per node kind
It agrees with emitted JS on the M1 Kernels it supports, or a note says why it stops at pure Kernels
It exposes a per-node evaluation hook carrying spans, for the debugger

data.title: The JS backend emits f32 and vectors
data.description:
Why: the JS backend is the stage and the pixel debugger's CPU path, and the proposal says it enforces a Dialect's numeric rules, including f32 rounding (§6).

What: kit/emit/js emits the new types: f32 operations rounded with Math.fround, vector operations in a representation the builder chooses (scalarized locals, arrays or typed arrays; record the choice and the reason in kit/emit/js/README.md), and the fields intrinsics in their JS spelling. A fields Kernel emits to a function the harness can call per pixel. The output agrees exactly with the reference interpreter where both exist (same rounding), which the harness leaf checks at scale; here, a test per new node kind.

Seams: kit/emit/js only. DMG emission must stay byte-identical (the emit goldens and the dmg-diff runs). Record any change to existing M1 code in a note, for H2.

criteria.label: f32, vector and fields-intrinsic nodes emit, with a test per node kind
The DMG emit tests and dmg-diff over 04–07 are unchanged

data.title: Decision: how the GLSL comparison runs outside a browser
data.description:
The question for Ben: agents test in Node, and Node has no WebGL. WebGL2 works inside an artifact page (M0), and the delivery rulings make the browser the baseline for checks, with Node as an extra.

Options:
(a) Page only. The comparison harness is kit code that runs in a page; agents check GLSL by opening that page in a browser (the built-in browser or Claude in Chrome) and reading its report. No new dependency; GLSL is never in `npm test`, so a regression is caught only when someone opens the page.
(b) A headless browser as a dev dependency (Playwright or Puppeteer driving headless Chromium, whose software GL renderer gives WebGL2 without a GPU). `npm test` or the prerelease suite runs the page and reads the report. One large dev dependency (a Chromium download), and the software renderer's floats may differ from a real GPU's, so the tolerance must hold on real hardware too.
(c) Both: (b) in the prerelease suite, and the page for real-GPU runs.

Recommendation: (c), with the dependency in devDependencies only and the headless run in the prerelease suite, so the fast suite stays dependency-free and fast.

Waiting on it: the GLSL half of the comparison harness. The GLSL backend itself can proceed, since its output can be unit-tested as text.

data.title: The first LIR stage and the GLSL backend
data.description:
Why: GLSL is the first backend with no host to lean on, so Ben ruled that it owns the first LIR stage, with an IR verifier after each lowering; wasm follows later on that LIR. A fields Kernel over `pixel` must become a GLSL ES 3.00 fragment shader (WebGL2, D3).

What: a lowering from the IR to an LIR (kit/lir/ or a name the builder argues for) in which what GLSL cannot leave implicit becomes explicit: no f64 (each f64 is narrowed explicitly, and a Kernel whose meaning depends on f64 precision is rejected with a diagnostic), explicit int/float conversions, intrinsics bound to their GLSL spelling. The verifier gains LIR rules and runs after the lowering. Then kit/emit/glsl/ emits a fragment shader: params as uniforms, `uv` from the fragment coordinate, the color to the output, and a line map from GLSL lines to spans (as the JS backend has). A Kernel the GLSL target cannot take (effects, an Iteration Space it does not accept) is refused with the proposal's capability message (§6, "Capabilities").

Seams: new kit directories; kit/ir/verify.js for LIR rules; the fields Dialect's GLSL spellings. Unit tests compare emitted text against goldens; running the shader is the harness leaf's job. Keep in mind the backlog's "IR stages below the core" entry: this LIR is that stage's first form, so name it and document it in its own README.

Out of scope: wasm, WGSL, integer stores (fields has none; if a survey sketch needs one, say so and stop).

criteria.label: The two survey Kernels lower to LIR that verifies and emit GLSL ES 3.00 with a line map, with golden tests
A Kernel GLSL cannot take is refused with a capability diagnostic, with a test

data.title: The comparison harness, JS and GLSL against the interpreter
data.description:
Why: this is M2's "done when": the same source drives both backends, and they agree with the reference. D5: floats within a tolerance the target declares, integers exactly.

What: a harness (library in kit/, runnable in a page; a thin CLI in scripts/ for Node) that evaluates a fields Kernel over a grid of pixels and a set of param values through the interpreter, the JS backend and GLSL (read back from a framebuffer), and reports the worst difference per pair, the pixel, and the source line. JS against the interpreter must match exactly. GLSL against the interpreter must fall within a tolerance the GLSL target declares; this leaf proposes the figure from measurement on the software renderer and, if possible, a real GPU, and records it. Planted faults (an operator swapped, a constant nudged, a component swizzled) must be caught: report how many and which escape, as M1 did for dmg-diff.

Seams: the interpreter, both backends, and the runner Ben chooses in the decision leaf. Record figures in an M2 findings draft with the command that reproduces each.

criteria.label: Both survey Kernels agree, JS against the interpreter exactly and GLSL within the declared tolerance, over a recorded grid and param set
The planted-fault run is recorded, with every escaped fault explained

data.title: The pixel debugger
data.description:
Why: the proposal promises "a pixel debugger for free" (§12): because every shader Kernel also has a CPU form, one pixel can be run and stepped through. It is part of M2's roadmap row.

What: given a fields Program, a pixel and params, step through the Kernel's evaluation node by node with each value and its source span, using the interpreter's evaluation hook. A library API in kit/ plus a preview page that renders the shader, lets a reader click a pixel, and shows the source with the current span highlighted and the values beside it (the Previews principle: the page also renders fixed states for review). Show where the interpreter's value and the GPU's differ, when the harness has a GPU value for that pixel.

Seams: the interpreter's hook, the GLSL backend for the image. Keep the library free of DOM code; the page is a thin consumer. Out of scope: skins and the workbench shell (M4).

criteria.label: The library steps one pixel through a Kernel with values and spans, with tests
A preview page shows a clicked pixel's trace over the highlighted source, checked in a browser with a screenshot in the leaf's notes

data.title: Port two sketches both ways and test H3
data.description:
Why: H3, "typed operators make shader code pleasant without confusing authors"; it fails if authors or models keep expecting plain-JS behavior. Ben ruled for typed operators (D1) before testing them, so this is the check on that ruling.

What: the two survey sketches written twice, as fields Programs with typed operators and as plain-JS `add(mul(…))` calls, compared on length, readability, and errors. Then the model test: fresh agents given only the fields Dialect's documentation write a few new sketches in each style; count the errors that come from expecting plain-JS semantics (a vector printed or compared as an object, `+` used for concatenation, an operator on mismatched types), and how the diagnostics guided the fix. Record the result in the M2 findings.

Open, the builder's call: how many fresh agents and sketches (enough to see a pattern; say how many and why). Which model writes them: say which, since the subject is models.

data.title: Fix the lowering review's findings: arity, TDZ, constant identity, enums, shared sites
data.description:
Why: an independent review (2026-11-23, of 96954db and e9515b3) confirmed ten defects in lowering with a probe, kit/lower/test/rhea-probe.test.js (kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-workbench/d340350f-8669-4079-ad13-a636f271f7f7/scratchpad/rhea-probe.test.js; its failing tests are the red tests for this leaf, minus the nested-literals one, which waits on Ben in its own decision leaf). Two of them make emitted code behave differently from the source, which is the class that must never happen.

What, each with its fault:
1. `[1, , 2]` crashes lowering (kit/lower/expr.js:468 lowers a null element). Give a diagnostic instead.
2. A helper's or method's arity comes from its first call site (kit/lower/callsites.js:27, call.js:205 and :238), so correct calls fail when the first is wrong, and the verdict depends on lambda order. Arity comes from the declaration; each wrong call is its own L015.
3. A name read in its own temporal dead zone (`const { a: x } = x`, `const [x] = x`, `for (const m of m)`, and the older `const x = x + 1`) lowers as a read of the outer name; the source throws ReferenceError. Reject it (kit/lower/stmt.js:88, :108, :121).
4. A baked list or struct constant is written out fresh at each use, so `D === D` emits `[1,2] === [1,2]` (false; the source gives true). Main thread's call: keep baking, and reject `===` and `!==` on list and struct values (L003, with a tip to compare fields), since identity of compound values has no meaning in a shader or C backend either. Then reconcile kit/lower/README.md (line 30) with the M1 plan's note that only number, string and boolean constants are baked: say what the code does.
5. One lambda shared by several entity kinds reports its conflict twice and names the same site twice (sites keyed by slot id and range, kit/lower/call.js:168, :183; the pipeline gives every user the same id). One error, at the second site, naming two distinct sites.
6. Enums always merge (kit/ir/types.js:108 strictJoin): a Dialect enum plus a non-member literal widens silently, and two different Dialect enums join. The ruling (M1 plan, "Subset widenings after M1") already says: Dialect types are nominal, and an enum meets a literal by membership. Two string literals still give their enum. The IR must tell a Dialect enum from one built from literals; the representation is the builder's call, documented in kit/ir/README.md.
7. A pure helper called inside a query callback is always L006 (kit/lower/lowerer.js:20: the `call f` effect is not pure). Judge it by the helper's own effects.
8. A helper that no runtime lambda reaches still contributes call sites, so declaration order decides whether a reached helper lowers. Only call sites in code reached from a runtime lambda count.
9. Nit: `null` joined with a void call gives a void parameter and a confusing L003 (kit/ir/types.js:96-104); make it an L014 naming both sites.
10. Nit: kit/lower/test/widen.test.js:153 "a hole skips an item" asserts only L008; also assert the emitted index. Doc nit: kit/lower/README.md line 29 "the first site's type stands" is false when a later site widens.

Seams: kit/lower (expr.js, callsites.js, call.js, stmt.js, lowerer.js, index.js, README), kit/ir/types.js and its README. Re-run `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js survey` and `diff --all-presets --seeds 7,11 --frames 1200`: 0 differences, and report any lambda whose status moved.

criteria.label: Every probe test except the nested-literals one passes as a regression test in the suite
The survey and diff --all-presets are re-run with 0 differences, and any status change is explained

data.title: Decision: do literals nested in a list or struct join across call sites?
data.description:
Question for Ben, from the lowering review (2026-11-23): should string literals nested in a list or struct join across call sites? Today `f({ d: "up" })` with `f({ d: "down" })`, `f(["a"])` with `f(["b"])` are L014, because the strict join's closed list only joins two literals at the top level ("same type" otherwise). `f([1])` with `f([1, 2])` is also L014, which follows from lists of different lengths not joining (job qL6eyA).

Options: (a) keep it: one rule, applied only at the top, fail fast (the strict-join ruling's spirit); (b) join structurally: two structs or lists join when their fields or items join under the same closed list, so nested literals give their enum. (b) is natural JS and still closed, but it makes the join recursive and its errors harder to name.

Recommendation: (b) for literals-to-enum inside structs and lists of the same length, and nothing else; the error names the field path. Waiting on it: nothing in M2; it would widen what the survey lowers only if a preset does this (none does today).
